findings.text: follow-on: the membership test set(bindings) <= comparison_expected_names counts a migration name at any stage, so a source bound to a live predecessor and a retired successor is classified as a dual-bound adjudicable conflict even though the branch's detail text asserts two live identities.

follow-on: SourceBindingConflictError has no production consumer — the graph and edit callers catch no name for it — so the retry-budget withholding the class docstring describes is not yet wired and every caller still treats both branches alike.

follow-on: for the dual-bound case holding_identity is set to old_name, the predecessor the migration is retiring, rather than an actual holder, so a consumer keying on holding_identity reads the retired name as the conflicting identity.

item_verdicts.diff: read 6ed434f45 against base 18d19d73; four files change — 29 lines adding an elif in retarget_standard_name_sources, the dual-bound test un-xfailed and rewritten to a typed raises, one new narrowness test, and the landing fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks that the dual-bound test pass with its xfail removed asserting SourceBindingConflictError naming the source and both identities, that a second test keep an unrelated compare-and-set failure on the anonymous RuntimeError, and that the provenance gate add no failures; the manifest records after_suite 69 passed EXIT=0 against baseline_suite 67 passed/1 xfailed EXIT=0, with negative_control.log EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to classify a source still bound to another live identity as the adjudicable binding conflict; imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py:645 adds the elif that classifies a source bound to both example_old_name and example_new_name as SourceBindingConflictError, reached through the compose supersede chain at graph_ops.py:7808.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; status complete, one landed revision 6ed434f45, a tests line naming the five gate files, test_logs naming baseline_suite.log, after_suite.log and negative_control.log, and negative_control_log a bare path whose header records the base revision and the module under test.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is provenance_lifecycle.py, tests/standard_names/test_compose_supersede_dual_bound.py, tests/standard_names/test_source_migration_conflict.py and the sib-dual-bound-conflict.html fragment; every path in the diff is one of those four.

justifications.durability: negative_control.log shows test_compose_supersede_over_dual_bound_source_raises_adjudicable_conflict reddens (EXIT=1) with provenance_lifecycle.py reverted, and the new test_single_live_binding_is_not_a_dual_bound_conflict reddens if the len(bindings)>1 bound at line 649 were relaxed.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's after_suite (69 passed, EXIT=0) and baseline_suite (67 passed, 1 xfailed, EXIT=0) bound the gate the done_when names and negative_control.log records EXIT=1, though the literal "both fail with the fix reverted" is met only by the dual-bound test since the narrowness test passes at base by design.
justifications.fit: the elif follows the surrounding branch idiom at imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py:624 and both added test names describe behaviour with no plan or gate label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py:645 fires exactly for a source whose compared live bindings are both migration names, the state the section's reproduction traced to the anonymous branch.
justifications.reuse: the branch reuses the existing SourceBindingConflict and binding_conflicts accumulator at imas_codex/standard_names/provenance_lifecycle.py:57, and a search for a prior dual-bound classifier found only its sibling _live_foreign_bindings at line 91.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff between base 18d19d73 and head 6ed434f45 is inside the four declared write paths.
